title: Animated characters in Rust: a rigged GLB on an animator, stood on the ground by its feet
note: Load a rigged GLB with gfx.character, start on Animator::simple, advance it only in on_update, and draw it at its capsule's feet with frame.character.
intent: A rigged GLB moves on the built-in animator, never a hand-rolled bone loop. In on_reset gfx.character(path) loads it (animation-asset-invalid: no usable skin or clips; hero.clip_names() lists the clips), and Animator::simple(&hero) is the start: .play(idle), .crossfade(walk, 0.25) every tick, .play_once(slash) for an attack. Move to hero.graph() only for parameters, layers or events. Only on_update advances it, with animator.update(ctx.dt); a draw or probe hook cannot. Stand it on the ground by its feet, never its centre: Character::spawn(&mut sim.physics, feet, CharacterParams::default()) puts a capsule there (Character::on_ground and drive_on a height function without physics); drive it with CharacterMotion::Velocity { wish, jump } and draw frame.character(&animator, character.transform().into()), so the model's feet are the capsule's. Probe Animator::probe and the feet's height beside the ground's so a check proves it moves and stands; capture it near and far.
port: The facet that owns a character owns its animator, its capsule and its probes; another facet sets the wish it walks by, never the animator.

evidence.note: gfx.character, Animator::simple's play, crossfade and play_once, update only in on_update, frame.character, Animator::probe.
Character::spawn at the feet, drive with CharacterMotion, character.transform().into() to draw, feet() to read; on_ground and drive_on without physics.
Moving things: gfx.character with an Animator for rigged models, Character::spawn for the body.
